rows.what the ink shows: The word between les and avec consists of an isolated low initial dot, two flattened horizontal bodies, a short cup, a connected low wavering body and an upturned terminal hook. At 4× the middle letter counters and the supposed accents are not independently recoverable. The visible skeleton is compatible with énoncés, but does not securely establish the whole word.

Inside the parentheses a short curved initial stroke and raised dot-like stroke precede an elongated low connector. Near its right end a small hook falls below the main body, followed by a short terminal e-shaped cup. The separate horizontal underline lies beneath these strokes; the sequence supports signe.

A rounded zero and comma survive. The stroke immediately before the zero is fused with its left side, so a separate opening bracket is not secure. The endpoint has a small left oval and an open-looking right bowl, but several heavy crossing strokes and a tall curved delimiter overlap its right side. Enlarged comparison with the page’s clear two-lobed infinity and open omega does not recover the obscured joins or delimiters; retain the interval uncertainty.

The terminal deleted word retains a small curved e-loop below the cancellation line, rising into a short tall t-stem that projects above it. The t cross stroke merges with the cancellation, but the lower e return and vertical t are distinct.

After the less-than sign, the final character has an oblique upper-left stroke and a rounded closed lower loop returning on the right across the cancellation. It is one pointed oval, with no second lobe or central crossing; the digit is 0.

The cancelled line has a clearly projecting tall f with a hooked lower turn near x527, a following i dot near x545, and a compressed connected low-letter ending, supporting finies. Before that f, the thick cancellation stroke merges the low curves and a peaked ascender of the proposed à valeurs; neither the initial accent nor the full letter sequence can be separated. The preceding line was also enlarged to verify the wrap after f et g sont.

The numeral after proposition is overwritten: a long hooked and crossed downstroke survives on the left, while an upper-right curved cap turns into a cusp and a lower diagonal. The clear 4s elsewhere on this page have an angular upper bend and short descending terminal, whereas the right-hand sweep here also admits a 5. Enlargement and the same-page 4/5 controls do not separate the layers sufficiently to decide which final numeral was intended.

La is visible at the preceding line end, with a tall L and a closed a loop. The next line preserves the initial small curves, raised marks and two pronounced p/q descenders of réciproque. At the end, the low v/r/a sequence and raised i dot support vraie. The cancellation bar merges most of the middle letter bodies; lower e-like curves and short joined remnants remain, but do not independently distinguish the full est encore sequence.

Under the heavy cancellation, the large opening C and paired tall ll ascenders identify Corollaire, matching the corresponding shapes in this page’s upper heading. To their right, the final tall hook descends into a basal rightward foot and stands beyond the low ending of the word. That hooked terminal is a separate 2, unlike the upper heading’s low final e; the source reading omits this numeral.
